page: Microsoft Azure E16pds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 hardware. It features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with one thread per core, delivering 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading contention. The system provides 128.0 GB of memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Architectural cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. For temporary storage, the instance bundles 644 GB of local SSD capacity. No GPUs are attached.

Benchmark evaluations position the E16pds_v5 within average mid-range performance tiers for multi-threaded and memory-intensive execution. Multi-core operations recorded 28,904.71 in stress-ng and 9,470.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing. Memory performance yields uncached read bandwidth of 122.17 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 65.4 GB/sec on 256 MB blocks, complementing a PassMark memory score of 1,883.14. Single-core evaluations reveal lower relative processing throughput, logging 1,087.0 on Geekbench single-core, 8.49 GB/sec on single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and 2,590.42 on the PassMark encryption test.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on high memory density and stable thread isolation over peak single-thread execution speed or advanced vector operations. The Neoverse-N1 architecture omits x86 extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX, which limits compute speed in heavy mathematical transformations and larger language model prompt processing, where 7B prompt parsing reached 19.03 tokens per second. However, for workloads requiring steady concurrency and abundant memory, the 16 dedicated physical cores prevent neighbor-thread interference across the 128.0 GB memory footprint.

The E16pds_v5 delivers cost-efficient memory scaling on ARM-native runtimes. With PassMark database operations reaching 10,869.44 and Redis achieving 21.74 million SET operations per second, it is well aligned for in-memory caches, relational or NoSQL database workloads, memory-intensive static web serving, and distributed ARM-based compilation environments requiring local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E16pds_v5 is an ARM-based memory-optimized virtual machine running on Ampere Neoverse-N1 silicon. Configured with 16 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz and 128.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation with 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes 644 GB of local SSD storage and operates without an attached GPU. Benchmark profiles indicate solid multi-threaded and memory throughput, including 21.74 million Redis SET operations per second and 122.17 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth. Although single-core speeds and vector acceleration are modest compared to x86 alternatives, its non-hyperthreaded core layout and large memory pool offer efficient resource density. It is suited for in-memory caching layers, relational databases, distributed ETL pipelines, and ARM-optimized microservices.
